_about: The key floor of spec 01 "Keys in memory and the lock", rule 4: an all-zero key is never a key. No legitimate key is all zeros, so a client refuses one before the platform's crypto provider is called. Hand-authored from the independent oracle in tools/vector-gen/oracle (Node WebCrypto and @noble; no andvari code), which applies the rule at these three operations. Regenerate with `npm run generate` there; `npm run check` fails on any difference.

refuse: one row per input that must be refused. `operation` names the operation (links.derive: links.json's `derive`; devicelink.derive: devicelink.json's `derive`; vaultlog.vkCommit: vaultlog.json's `vkCommit.derive`), `refusedAt` says where in it the refusal falls, and `input` holds the operation's inputs under the names that file's rows use. expect.refused = true: the operation gives no value at all; in the shared code it throws KeysGoneException, never a derived value and never an error that reads as a wrong key or damaged data. `formerly` names the normative row that carried this input until 2026-11-16, before the rule; its place there holds the near-zero input (31 zero bytes and one 0x01), the lowest input the floor accepts, derived as an ordinary row.

These rows grade the derivation itself. Where the same zeros arrive as data, rule 4 refuses them where they are read, as what they are: a link or device link whose secret is zeros is a bad link (bad_link), and a zero key matches no vault-key commitment (the check of a candidate key, vaultlog.json's `vkCommit.check`, answers false for it; it does not throw). Those answers belong to the files that grade reading links and checking keys, and none of their rows holds a zero key today.

refuse.name: links-derive-zero-secret
refuse.why: A link secret of 32 zero bytes. Nothing is derived from it: not linkId, offerKey, answerKey, registerToken or tokenHash. Rule 4: an HKDF input key of zeros is refused before the platform's provider is called; a link whose secret is zeros is a bad link where the link is read.
refuse.refusedAt: the link derivation of design section 2.3 (secret -> linkId, offerKey, answerKey, registerToken), before its first HKDF
refuse.formerly: links.json derive[2], until 2026-11-16; that place now holds the near-zero secret (31 zero bytes and one 0x01)

refuse.name: devicelink-derive-zero-secret
refuse.why: A device-link secret of 32 zero bytes. Nothing is derived from it: not linkId or macKey. Rule 4: an HKDF input key of zeros is refused before the platform's provider is called; a device link whose secret is zeros is a bad link where the link is read, and a device-link MAC under wiped link keys is refused.
refuse.refusedAt: the device-link derivation of design sections 2.3 and 8 (secret -> linkId, macKey), before its first HKDF
refuse.formerly: devicelink.json derive[2], until 2026-11-16; that place now holds the near-zero secret (31 zero bytes and one 0x01)

refuse.name: vaultlog-vkcommit-zero-key
refuse.why: A vault key of 32 zero bytes. No commitment is computed from it. Rule 4: an HKDF input key of zeros is refused before the platform's provider is called, and a zero key matches no vault-key commitment.
refuse.refusedAt: the vault-key commitment of design section 3.4 (hexLower(HKDF(VK, "andvari/v2|vk-commit|" + vaultId))), before the HKDF
refuse.formerly: vaultlog.json vkCommit.derive[3], until 2026-11-16; that place now holds the near-zero key (31 zero bytes and one 0x01)
